title: kv-cache: improved memory management and eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation, paging, and spillover
author: Aisha Fernandes
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and suboptimal eviction ordering has been causing increased GPU memory paging and spillover to host memory under mixed-workload traffic. This PR introduces a set of coordinated changes to the runtime KV cache memory manager: 1) compacting defragmentation pass that runs opportunistically when free segments fall below a threshold, 2) LRU+weighted recency eviction that prefers evicting long-lived low-reuse entries over recently accessed ones, 3) paging-aware admission control to avoid admitting very large KV entries when device free < X%, and 4) spillover batching to reduce thrash when spilling to host (grouped async transfers + prioritization). The description below lists the behavioral changes, implementation notes, tests, and migration considerations. Implementation notes: the defrag pass is incremental and lock-free for the hot path; it registers candidate segments and does multi-frame compaction on a background worker to avoid p99 spikes. Eviction policy is now a two-stage scorer (recency_score, size_penalty, reuse_boost) and exposes tuning knobs via runtime config. Paging admission uses a soft and hard threshold (soft: 25% free, hard: 10% free) with exponential backoff on admission failures. Spillover batching groups pages by liveness and issues coalesced CUDA host transfers; it also adds a small adaptive delay to aggregate small spills. Tests: unit tests for scoring and rationale, large e2e perf regression tests on the perf-canary harness (simulating mixed short/long contexts), and an integration test that intentionally fragments device memory to confirm compaction reduces host paging. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime config kv.defrag.enabled=false by default in this release; opt-in for Dedicated clusters for canary. Related Linear: ENG-1987, ENG-2139. See also a follow-up PR that exposes two tuning knobs in the console.

review_conversation: Marco Rivera (reviewer): Can you explain why the defrag pass is safe without a global stop-the-world? I'm worried about concurrent reads during compaction.

Aisha Fernandes (author): The defrag is implemented with pointer indirection: entries reference an immutable handle that we update via atomic CAS once compaction completes for a segment. Readers always dereference the handle, so they see either old or new location; we never free the old pages until all outstanding readers indicate completion via epoch counters. Added more comments and a unit test to verify reader safety.
Sofia Patel (reviewer): The eviction scorer has a size_penalty term that can bias toward freeing many small entries instead of a few large ones — did you benchmark the impact on throughput?

Aisha Fernandes (author): Yes — added perf-canary scenarios. The weighted scorer defaults were tuned to prefer evicting large entries when they exceed 2x median size; we measured 8-12% tail latency improvement on mixed workloads and 15% reduction in host paging events.
Jared Kim (reviewer): Suggest exposing the soft/hard thresholds via console for Dedicated customers. Also flag this behind runtime feature flag until we validate metrics.
Aisha Fernandes (author): Agreed — added config knobs and feature flagging. Console exposure will be a follow-up PR to avoid coupling rollout timelines.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: opportunistic defragmentation, paging-aware admission control, improved eviction heuristics, and spillover batching to reduce host paging and tail latency. Feature-gated; opt-in for Dedicated canaries.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover scorer and allocator invariants. Integration test simulates fragmentation and asserts reduced host paging and lower p99 latency. Perf-canary harness run against two cluster sizes (c4-large, c4-xlarge) with mixed context lengths. Monitoring: added new metrics kv.defrag.compactions, kv.eviction.score_histogram, kv.spill.batch_size.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged off by default. Step 1: enable for internal Dedicated canaries (10 clusters) for 2 weeks. Step 2: enable for >50% internal traffic if no regressions. Step 3: expose tuning knobs in Redwood Console and allow customer opt-in.
notes_for_ops: If you see increased cpu worker utilization during compaction windows, lower kv.defrag.max_background_ops or increase kv.defrag.min_free_segments. Emergency rollback: set kv.defrag.enabled=false and flush worker queues; eviction policy can be reverted via kv.eviction.policy=legacy_lru.
